title: Homomorphisms and existential-positive formulas
summary: Positive formulas survive homomorphisms; compactness proves that every first-order sentence with this preservation property has an existential-positive description.
abstract: A directed path can be mapped to a single loop: its edges survive even when its vertices merge. Such maps are homomorphisms. In general structures they preserve the named operations and constants, and send true relation instances forward. Formulas built from atomic facts using conjunction, disjunction and existential witnesses survive these maps too, because each witness can be sent to its image. The converse is equally precise: a first-order sentence preserved by every homomorphism between nonempty structures is equivalent to a sentence of this existential-positive form. This connects a semantic question about which maps preserve a property with an exact restriction on how that property can be described. Inequalities and requirements about every target point show why the restriction matters.
